turns.assessment: The simultaneous, network-wide loss began at t=602.5 and is accompanied by OCH LOS and loss of optical input on multiple directions leaving S01. Every affected working path depends on roadm.S01 (E1), while a client-port, transponder, amplifier, or OTN-switch failure would not explain this shared optical blast radius. A hard WSS input-port failure at S01 best fits; attenuation or filter drift would affect only one channel and generally would not produce broad LOS.

proposals.rationale: E1 (roadm.S01) is the sole common dependency of all affected working paths. A failed WSS input port can block every channel arriving on the affected degree and generate the observed simultaneous downstream OCH and amplifier-input LOS across multiple onward directions.
A disconnected OMS input patch could create hard all-channel loss on one section, but it does not naturally explain the common multi-direction service impact as well as the shared S01 ROADM failure.
A switch-fabric failure could interrupt many ODUs at S01, but it would produce ODU-layer AIS rather than the extensive optical OCH and amplifier-input LOS evidence.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode

clarify.assessment: The evidence localizes the failure to roadm.S01 but does not identify one failed ingress degree. AMP_INPUT_LOS on multiple outgoing sections indicates loss after S01 switching, while the supplied observations do not uniquely distinguish among the five candidate WSS input ports. Selecting one would risk a wrong repair.

llm_alone.decision: commit not to one place (5 locations); reported as a set

score.why: truth not in the reported set
